question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=99$ from a population where $45%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that less than $50%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8159\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ | $\,0.8238\,$ |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8413\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ | $\,0.8485\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8643\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ | $\,0.8708\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=99,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.45.$

Now, since

$$
np=99(0.45)=44.55>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=99(1-0.45)=54.45>5,
$$

and $n=99$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.45,\frac{0.45(1-0.45)}{99}) \\  & ∼N(0.45,0.0025).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}<0.5).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}<0.5) & =P(Z<\frac{0.5-0.45}{\sqrt{0.0025}}) \\  & =P(Z<1.00) \\  & =Φ(1.00).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.00) & =0.8413.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}<0.5) & =Φ(0.8413) \\  & =0.8413.\end{aligned}
$$
